what: The card or payment method was refused. Ask for another one. Returned, not thrown, by the provider calls that charge or check a card. `providerCode` is the provider's own code, such as Stripe's `card_declined` or `expired_card`; `declineCode` is the bank's reason when it gave one.
fix: Ask the customer for another card or payment method. The same one is likely refused again.

what: The host app's setup of a payments service cannot work: a capability a configured step needs was not passed, or a setting is empty or malformed. Thrown when the service is built (at boot), never returned later as a silent no-op.
fix: Pass the capability or setting that `setting` names when the app builds the service.

what: A new customer clashes with a stored one: the user already has a customer with another provider id (`existingCustomerId` is that customer), or the provider id belongs to another user's customer (`existingCustomerId` is null). Nothing was written.
fix: Use the user's stored customer (`findCustomerByUserId`), or check which user the provider customer belongs to.

what: No customer segment has this id.
fix: Check the segment id; list the segments to find it.

what: The campaign exists but is not active, so it cannot run. Nothing was written.
fix: Set the campaign status to `active` first.

what: No dunning campaign has this id.
fix: Check the campaign id; list the campaigns to find it.

what: The campaign is active but has no active step (template) to send. Nothing was written.
fix: Add a step to the campaign, or activate one of its steps.

what: A campaign update removes a step that already sent a communication. The sent message keeps its step (its history points at it), so the update was refused and nothing changed.
fix: Keep the step in `templates` (change its content or delay instead), or deactivate the campaign and create a new one.

what: The payment already has a refund waiting for a decision. Nothing was written.
fix: Approve or reject the pending refund first.

what: A plan change was asked to take effect outside the subscription's current period. Times are ISO instants.
fix: Pick an effective date between `periodStart` and `periodEnd`, or leave it out to mean now.

what: The same idempotency key was used with different parameters. Returned by the calls that take an `idempotencyKey`.
fix: Use a new idempotency key for a different request, or resend the first request unchanged.

what: A webhook delivery's signature does not match the body and the webhook secret: it was not sent by the provider, the body changed after signing, the signature header is missing or malformed, or the signature timestamp is outside the tolerance. Returned by `StripeProvider.constructWebhookEvent`.
fix: Answer the delivery with HTTP 400. Check the webhook secret, and pass the raw request body, not re-serialized JSON.

what: A dunning step uses a channel that has no provider registered in this app. The communication was not written.
fix: Configure the channel in `createCommunicationOrchestrationService` (or `registerProvider`), or change the step's channel.

what: A notification was not delivered: the mail transport returned a failure (the `cause`), the Slack webhook answered with a non-2xx `status`, or the request failed or timed out (the `cause`).
fix: Check the transport or the Slack webhook URL and its status page, then send the notification again.

what: The notification provider answered with an error status (4xx or 5xx). The message was not sent. `upstreamMessage` is the provider's own error text when its body had one.
fix: Read `upstreamStatus` and `upstreamMessage`: a 4xx is our request (recipient, sender, key); a 5xx is the provider's fault and a later retry can work.

what: The notification provider answered with a success status, but the body is not the shape its API documents. The message may have been sent. `cause` holds the schema failure.
fix: Check the provider's API version and its status page; read `cause` for the field that did not match.

what: The notification provider did not answer within the provider's `timeoutMs`. The message may or may not have been sent.
fix: Retry later, or raise `timeoutMs` in the provider config.

what: A webhook recipient URL names a host that is not on the operator's `allowedHosts` list. Nothing was sent. The URL comes from customer metadata, so only hosts the operator listed may be reached.
fix: Add the host to `webhook.allowedHosts` if the operator trusts it, or correct the customer's `webhookUrl`.

what: An automatic payment (`automatic: true`, charged with the customer absent) was asked for without a `paymentMethodId`. Returned by `createPaymentIntent` before any provider request.
fix: Pass the saved payment method to charge, or use `automatic: false` and let the customer finish in the client.

what: The payment belongs to no subscription, so there is no subscription to keep alive with retries. Nothing was scheduled.
fix: Retry a one-off payment by asking the customer to pay again.

what: The two plans of a plan change are priced in different currencies, so a credit on one cannot be set against a charge on the other.
fix: Move the subscription to a plan in the same currency, or cancel it and start a new one.

what: The plan exists but is no longer offered (`isActive` is false). Nothing was sent to the provider or written.
fix: Pick an active plan (`findActivePlans`).

what: The provider price a plan row points at is not a flat recurring price (a tiered, metered or one-time price), so it has no single amount and interval to read a plan from. The price comes from the provider, so this is outside data, not a bug. Returned by `getPlan`, `updatePlan` and `listPlans`.
fix: Point the plan at a flat recurring price in the provider dashboard, or remove the price's `planId` metadata.

what: A Stripe price id that is not one of the subscription preset's `prices`. Returned by `createCheckoutSession` before any provider request, and by `handleWebhook` for a subscription on a price the app does not sell, so no plan nobody configured is granted.
fix: Add the price to `prices` with the plan row it sells, or check the price id the client sent.

what: A customer, plan, payment or subscription id has no row (`missing: 'row'`), or the row has no provider id (`missing: 'provider_id'`, such as a plan without a Stripe price). Returned before any provider request is made.
fix: Check the id, or create the row with the provider first.

what: The refund and what the payment already gives back add up to more than was paid. Amounts are decimal text in `currency`, such as `'12.50'`. Nothing was written.
fix: Ask for at most the refundable amount.

what: The refund is in another currency than the payment. A refund pays back the payment's own money, so it must be in the payment's currency. Nothing was written.
fix: Ask for the refund in `paymentCurrency`.

what: The refund was already decided, so it can no longer be approved or rejected. Nothing was written.
fix: Read the refund again to see its decision. Only a pending refund can be approved or rejected.

what: No refund has this id.
fix: Check the refund id.

what: The payment is older than the refund window. Nothing was written.
fix: Refund it outside this workflow, or not at all. The default window is 90 days (`refundWindowMs`).

what: A payment's stored `taxAmount` metadata cannot be added up: it is not `Money` JSON (`problem: 'not_money'`), or it is in another currency than the payment (`'other_currency'`). A wrong total must not pass, so the report stops here.
fix: Correct the payment's `metadata.taxAmount` to `Money` JSON in the payment's currency.

what: The user already has an active subscription, so a second one is not created. Nothing was sent to the provider or written.
fix: Change the plan of the existing subscription instead (`updateSubscription`).

what: The subscription's status does not allow the change: an update or a pause needs `active`, a resume needs `paused`, a reactivation needs `canceled` or `past_due`, and a canceled subscription cannot be canceled or flagged again. Nothing was sent to the provider or written.
fix: Read the subscription again and ask only for a change its status allows.

what: A provider subscription event has no subscription items, so it has no price and no billing period to store. Returned by `handleWebhook` and `projectStripeSubscription` before anything is written.
fix: Check the subscription in the provider dashboard: a Stripe subscription always has at least one item.

what: A customer address given for a tax calculation has no country, so no tax jurisdiction can be found. Returned by `calculateTax` and `createTaxTransaction` before any provider request.
fix: Ask for the customer's country, or leave the address out to use the one the provider holds.

what: A tax line is in another currency than the transaction it belongs to. Nothing was recorded and the provider was not called.
fix: Pass the breakdown that `calculateTax` returned for this transaction, in its currency.

what: No tax configuration, jurisdiction or exemption has this id. Nothing was written.
fix: Check the id. Read the row first if it may have been deleted.

what: A tax refund names no recorded sale to reverse: `originalReference` is missing (`null` here), or no sale was recorded under it. Nothing was recorded and the provider was not called.
fix: Record the sale first, and pass its `reference` as `originalReference`.

what: The payment to refund does not exist. Nothing was written.
fix: Check the payment id.

what: A provider subscription event names a provider customer with no local customer row, so no user owns it. The row is made at checkout; a subscription made outside checkout (in the Stripe dashboard) has none. Returned by `projectStripeSubscription` before anything is written.
fix: Start subscriptions through `createCheckoutSession`, or create the customer row for the provider customer first.

what: A provider subscription status this package does not model, such as one Stripe added after this release. Returned by `projectStripeSubscription` instead of guessing a status.
fix: Upgrade `@arki/payments`, or add the status to `subscriptionStatusValues`.

what: The claim insert conflicted, yet no row holds the event's provider id: the new webhook id collided with another row's, or the winning row was deleted between the two queries. Nothing was processed.
fix: Nothing; a resend claims the event again with a new webhook id.

what: No webhook event has this id. Nothing was written.
fix: Check the webhook event id. Ids come from `claimWebhookEvent` or `findWebhookEventByProviderEventId`.

what: Another delivery of the same event is running it now, inside its lease. This copy did not run it. Not a success: if the running attempt crashes, only a resend processes the event.
fix: Nothing; answer non-2xx so the provider resends later.

what: The event body does not have the fields the handler reads: no `id` or `type`, or a `data.object` that does not match the event type (a Stripe subscription with no items, a PaymentIntent with no id). `cause` holds the schema's `InvalidInput` when a schema refused it.
fix: Nothing to do per event; a resend carries the same body. Check the provider's API version if it repeats.

what: The webhook validator refused the delivery: a bad or missing signature, a source address that is not allowed, a timestamp outside the window, a replayed delivery, or no webhook secret. `reason` is the validator's own text, for logs only; branch on the code. Nothing was stored.
fix: Check the webhook secret and the provider's signing setup. A resend of the same delivery is refused again.

what: The event has been attempted `maxRetries` times and every attempt failed. The handler gives up, so the provider is told to stop resending.
fix: Read the stored `errorMessage` of the webhook event, fix its cause, then replay the event by hand.

what: The event is about a payment or subscription with no local row for its provider id. Retryable on purpose: the provider can send the webhook before the app's own insert of that row commits, and a later resend then finds it. A subscription made outside the app keeps failing until `maxRetries` gives it up (`WebhookRetriesExhausted`); no owner is invented.
fix: Nothing for a row about to commit. For a payment or subscription made outside the app, create it locally first.
